title: Suspension and comparison of coefficient data in minimal envelopes
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme and $a\in X$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A minimal smooth local envelope $X\hookrightarrow M$ at $a$ is a closed embedding in a smooth scheme for which the ambient cotangent space maps isomorphically to that of $X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Put $H_0=H_X(a)$ [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant]. Such envelopes exist after restriction and etale localization [def-weil-etale-morphism]. In one such envelope, supply regular Hilbert coefficient data on $N\hookrightarrow M$ [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum], and the ideal $I=\sum(c_{i\gamma}^{b/(d_i-|\gamma|)})$ for a positive common multiple $b$, with $(I,b)=(0,1)$ for an empty list [pqf-def-coherent]. Assume its finite-test cosupports agree with the loci retaining $H_0$ in the precise presentation sense [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]. If $a$ is singular (its local ring is not a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]), the transverse rank $r=\operatorname{codim}_M N$ of these essential coefficient variables is positive. In etale transverse retraction coordinates $p:M\to N$, $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, the explicit coherent ideal
$$J=(z_1^b,\ldots,z_r^b)+p^*I\subset\mathcal O_M$$
has the same finite tests as $(N,I,b)$ and order exactly $b$ throughout its cosupport [def-trf-marked-ideal-order]. For a regular codimension-zero germ, $(M,0,1)$ still presents the level, but its ideal has infinite order; no finite-order assertion is made for this case.
Given two minimal envelopes of the same pointed intrinsic germ and any two coefficient constructions as above (allowing the displayed suspensions), there is a common pointed etale comparison identifying the embedded copies of $X$ and $H_0$ on which the two marked data have the same finite tests. This comparison may retain any specified finite ordered list of intrinsic earlier-center ideal sheaves by actual ideal pullback [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. More precisely, after any two finite admissible histories whose transformed intrinsic germs, retained levels and ordered earlier-center ideals are so identified, the induced ordered boundary data and subsequent finite-test presentation classes are identified on the comparison. The earlier centers are history data and do not become the newly started test boundary, which is empty. The assertion is independence of a test-equivalence class, not equality or uniqueness of the coefficient ideals, and commutes with restriction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-embedding-etale-comparison] over $k=\mathbf Q$. Its minimality condition is precisely the cotangent-space condition in the statement, and it supplies a minimal envelope after restriction and etale localization. Applied to the supplied smooth closed pair $N\hookrightarrow M$, it also supplies the etale retraction and transverse parameters used in the displayed formula. The statement is local, so replace the neighbourhood by these pointed neighbourhoods throughout. The initial ordered test boundary is empty, and hence imposes no coordinate condition on this retraction.

source.place: VIII Remarks 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, background only; agent assembly of the cited local geometric and finite-test statements.

proof.text: We claim $r>0$ at a singular point. If $r=0$, the transverse multi-index set is $\mathbf N^0=\{0\}$. A nonempty vertex list would therefore have vertex $0$ and degree $d_i=0$. Condition (1) of [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum] makes $f_{i,b_0}$ a unit, whereas it belongs to the Taylor ideal of $X$ at its point $a$. That ideal is proper: evaluation at the origin kills all equations of $X$. This is impossible. The list is consequently empty; condition (3), generation of the Taylor ideal, then makes that ideal zero. The Taylor map of the smooth ambient local ring is faithfully flat by [lem-trf-diagonal-taylor-faithful-flatness]. Contracting the zero extended defining ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] shows that the defining stalk ideal of $X\times_MU$ at $a_U$ is zero. Descend to $M$: the stalk map $\mathcal O_{M,i(a)}\to\mathcal O_{U,a_U}$ of the etale $e$ is flat by [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] (with the module $\mathcal O_{U,a_U}$, flat over itself) and local, hence faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat]. The ideal of $X\times_MU$ at $a_U$ is the extension $K\mathcal O_{U,a_U}$ of the defining stalk ideal $K$ of $X$ at $a$, since affinely $(A/K)\otimes_AC=C/KC$. Contracting once more gives $K=0$. Thus $\mathcal O_{X,a}=\mathcal O_{M,i(a)}$, which is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], contradicting singularity. This also handles nonclosed $a$: the cited Taylor map uses residue-field base change at the diagonal point, not an identification of the ordinary completion with a power-series ring having all the relative variables.

source.place: VIII Remarks 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, background only; agent assembly of the cited local geometric and finite-test statements.

proof.text: First justify coherence without enumerating coefficient multi-indices. Both the coefficient scheme N and its etale ambient U are smooth over a field, hence locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. For any ideal sheaf on either scheme, its module is the kernel of the map from the structure sheaf to the closed-immersion pushforward of the quotient structure sheaf. The latter is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh], so the ideal module is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Every ideal of an affine Noetherian section ring is finitely generated; [lem-pqf-finite-type-ideal-module] converts this to finite type of the ideal module. This proves both markedCoefficientIdeal_coherent and suspendedCoefficientIdeal_coherent for the actual displayed ideals. The supplied $I$ is coherent and $b>0$. Apply [lem-trf-marked-ideal-transverse-suspension] in the neighbourhood of step 1, with empty boundary. It gives the actual ideal $J=(z_1^b,\ldots,z_r^b)+p^*I$, equality of cosupports and equivalence of every finite test, including the controlled-transform and ordinary-pullback conventions separately. Thus $J$ presents the same retained Hilbert--Samuel level because $(N,I,b)$ does so by hypothesis. At a singular point step 2 gives $r\ge1$, so the same theorem gives order exactly $b$ everywhere on cosupport. No assertion that the coefficient ideal on $N$ itself has finite order is used; in particular this argument permits $I=0$.

source.place: VIII Remarks 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, background only; agent assembly of the cited local geometric and finite-test statements.

proof.text: For a regular codimension-zero germ, restrict to $X=M$. Take the empty coefficient list, $N=M$, $I=0$ and $b=1$. Its Taylor ideal is zero, so the five conditions of the regular coefficient datum reduce to the unique zero quotient and the identity remainder; all empty Jacobian determinants are $1$. The jet-dimension identity of [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] identifies its Hilbert--Samuel function with the monomial-count function for the zero diagram, constant on this smooth chart. Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-test-sequence-propagation] to this empty datum: it supplies the equality after every finite test, including a summation after each line product. Hence $(M,0,1)$ is a presentation. Its ideal order is infinite by [def-trf-marked-ideal-order], not $1$. This use of the propagation statement satisfies its upper-bound hypothesis because the function is constant on the chosen smooth chart.

proof.text: For two minimal envelopes, [lem-trf-smooth-embedding-etale-comparison] gives a common pointed etale neighbourhood of closed pairs inducing the specified identification of $X$. Its compatibility with specified ideals preserves the finite ordered list of earlier-center ideal sheaves by actual ideal pullback. Pull the two coefficient constructions to this neighbourhood. They remain presentations: the smooth-pullback assertion of [lem-trf-coefficient-test-sequence-propagation] applies with relative dimension $0$, so the level stays $H_0$; equivalence under suspension follows from step 3. Consequently, at the initial stage both cosupports equal the same intrinsic equality locus. No equality of the two coherent coefficient ideals is asserted.

source.place: VIII Remarks 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, background only; agent assembly of the cited local geometric and finite-test statements.

proof.text: In that common ambient neighbourhood, induct on test depth $n$ using the recursive definition in [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]. Depth zero is the equality just proved. At any shared admissible prefix the two presentation hypotheses identify both cosupports with the retained-level locus of the same transformed $X$. Their next smooth centers are therefore exactly the same closed smooth centers satisfying the same normal-crossings condition against the same ordered test boundary. The ambient blowup and scheme-theoretic strict transform depend on this specified center, not on the coefficient ideal. Each presentation supplies its own controlled transform, and both have the intrinsic retaining-level cosupport there. For a line product the common transformed scheme and level are the same product and summed level, and both append the same zero section. For an intersection blowup the two selected labelled components specify the same center and both use ordinary pullback. These three cases prove the induction step, including existence of every required next transform. Quantification over $n$ gives the asserted test-equivalence class.

source.place: VIII Remarks 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, background only; agent assembly of the cited local geometric and finite-test statements.

proof.text: Apply steps 1 and 5--6 at a compared transformed intrinsic germ, with its retained level and its specified ordered earlier-center ideals. History retains the structure maps and the chronological ideal centers, even when an intrinsic blowup is an identity, as in [def-trf-admissible-embedded-history]. The induced boundary record is compared in this order: on the chart of a blowup distinguished by $e$, the new exceptional ideal is the extension of that stage's center ideal, namely $(e)$ by [lemma-nagata-chart-extended-ideal-principal]. Retain the strict transforms of the previous labelled components, each the scheme-theoretic closure off the new center as in [def-nagata-strict-transform] and hence determined by the identified diagram, and append this birth-stage ideal. Only where the center is a normal-crossings coordinate subspace in a regular chart are these the coordinate formulas of [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart], including empty components; the comparison does not use those formulas. Thus identical chronological ideal-pullback data give the identical induced intrinsic boundary record. At the compared current stage, the minimal-envelope comparison preserves each of the specified ideals. The subsequent presentation tests nevertheless restart with empty boundary, exactly as required in [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]; step 6 compares these tests. In particular we do not replace the earlier-center record by just the supports of its ideals or drop identity stages. All comparisons commute with restriction: restrict the pointed comparisons and their ideal equalities, and apply the same finite-depth induction on the restricted neighbourhood.
